question.prompt: Six points on a circle are given. Four of the chords joining pairs of the six points are selected at random. What is the probability that the four chords form a convex quadrilateral?

solutions.explanation:
Count unordered selections of chords, since the order of selection does not affect whether they form a quadrilateral. Each pair of the six points determines one chord, so there are
\[
\binom62=15
\]
chords. The total number of equally likely selections is therefore
\[
\binom{15}{4}
=\frac{15\cdot14\cdot13\cdot12}{4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}
=1365.
\]
To count favorable selections, choose four of the six points. Joining them in their order around the circle gives exactly one convex quadrilateral. No three circle points are collinear, so this quadrilateral is nondegenerate.

Conversely, every favorable selection consists of the four boundary sides of a convex quadrilateral and determines its four vertices. Thus every favorable selection comes from one four-point subset, and different vertex subsets cannot give the same chord selection. There are exactly
\[
\binom64=15
\]
favorable selections.

The probability is
\[
\frac{15}{1365}=\boxed{\frac1{91}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Count quadrilaterals by their vertices
